title: Hog Bait That Deer Won't Eat? Check Visitors on Camera
content:
TL;DR: If you want hog bait that deer won't eat, do not start with a new mix. Put the camera on the bait and see who is actually there. Separate deer visits from sounder commitment, and send a closure command only when the full sounder is inside.

Hog bait that deer won't eat is the wrong first question if you have not watched the site. The useful question is who is on the bait, how long they stay, and whether the sounder is committed inside the trap. The camera answers that. A guess about ingredients does not.

See Who Is on the Bait

Mount the wild hog trap camera system so the bait, the entry, and the edge of the trap are in one live view. You need inside and outside the trap.

Review more than one night before you change anything. Note the time, the species you can actually see, and whether animals fed or only circled. Fresh rooting, trails, wallows, and rubs still tell you hogs are using the property. They do not tell you who emptied last night's bait.

A HogEye steel camera is built for that trap-site read: live video, day or night, with digital pan, tilt, and zoom so you can check the edge without another drive.

Deer Visits and Sounder Commitment Are Different

Deer on the bait are a timing problem, not a reason to invent a secret mix. If deer are cleaning the site before hogs arrive, you will watch an empty trap and blame the bait. If hogs are feeding and deer are only passing, the pile is already doing its job.

Use the live feed to separate those patterns:

  • Deer in daylight, hogs after dark
  • One or two animals testing the edge, then leaving
  • A sounder entering, feeding, and settling inside
  • Animals still outside the trap while others are on the bait

Do not close because the pile looks used. Close when your closure criteria are met: the complete sounder is inside and settled. Partial capture educates the hogs that stayed outside. Those survivors get trap-shy, and the program slips for months.

Wild hog behavior and trap timing is the backdrop. The feed is the evidence for this site, this week.

Change the Site Only After the Feed Is Clear

Hold the bait steady while you learn the pattern. Swapping materials every night teaches you nothing, because you changed two variables at once. Keep the same bait, keep the camera fixed, and give the sounder several nights to show a repeatable visit.

Move the site only when video supports it: deer clear the bait before the sounder arrives, hogs will not commit, or the camera still cannot see the edge. An empty pile with no identifiable visit is a placement problem until the feed shows otherwise. Common hog trap mistakes include closing early and trusting a morning walk over the night the animals were there.

This is not a bait recipe. Before you stake a trap line on any specific bait claim, ask for a source you can check.

What the Camera Is For at a Baited Trap

The HogEye job at a baited site is remote trap monitoring and closure. Watch the live video. Count the sounder. Confirm that the animals outside are accounted for. Then you send the closure command. The camera does not decide, and it does not close the gate by itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if deer are eating the hog bait?

Watch the live feed across several nights. The pile cannot name the visitor. Log species, time, and whether animals stayed inside the trap.

Should I change bait because deer are on the site?

Not on the first sighting. Keep the bait steady until the pattern is clear. Change the site plan when video shows deer clearing it before the sounder commits, or when hogs never commit.

When do I close the trap?

When the complete sounder is inside and settled. A used bait pile is not a closure signal. You send the closure command. The camera does not close the gate on its own.

Check the Visitors, Then Decide

Hog bait that deer won't eat is a visitor question. See who is on the bait, keep the bait steady while you learn, and close only for a full sounder. That is how a baited trap stays a capture tool instead of a guessing game.
